 Order

Dated this the 12th day of April, 2024 Accused Nos.1 to 3 in Crime No.320/2024 of Adoor Police Station, Pathanamthitta seek the relief of anticipatory bail in this petition filed under Section 438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure.
2. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioners and the learned Public Prosecutor.
Perused the relevant documents form part of the case diary in detail.

3. The precise form of the prosecution allegation is that the marriage between the defacto complainant and the first accused was solemnized on 24.04.2016 and thereafter, the defacto complainant resided along with accused Nos.1 to 3 at the matrimonial home.
According to the defacto complainant, during her stay at the matrimonial home, she was subjected to cruelty by demanding more dowry.
Thus, the prosecution alleges commission of offences punishable under Sections 498A and 323 read with Section 34 of IPC. BAIL APPL. NO. 2595 OF 2024 4.

According to the learned counsel for the petitioners, the first accused is a heart patient undergoing treatment for the same, as could be borne out from Annexure 2 medical records, and the allegations against the petitioners are false.
He offered cooperation in the matter of investigation while canvassing anticipatory bail.

5. Though the learned Public Prosecutor formally opposed grant of bail, no serious overt acts,
warranting custodial interrogation of the petitioners, could be foreseeable from the records.
Therefore, effective investigation is possible even without custodial interrogation .

Therefore, I am inclined to enlarge the petitioners on bail by directing the petitioners to subject themselves to interrogation.
Therefore, this petition stands allowed.

The petitioners are enlarged on anticipatory bail on the following conditions:
i.

The petitioners shall surrender before the Investigating Officer within ten days from today and on such surrender, the BAIL APPL. NO. 2595 OF 2024 Investigating Officer can question the petitioners and record their statement.
In the event of their arrest, the Investigating Officer shall produce the petitioners before the Jurisdictional Court on the date of arrest itself.

ii. On such production, Jurisdictional Court shall release the petitioners on bail, on executing bond for Rs.30,000/- (Rupees thirty thousand) each by themselves and by two solvent sureties, each for the like sum to the satisfaction of the Jurisdictional Court.
iii. The petitioners shall co-operate with investigation and shall be made available for interrogation and for the purpose of investigation, as and when the Investigating Officer directs so.
